title: Fast End-to-End Simulation and Exploration of Many-RISCV-Core Baseband Transceivers for Software-Defined Radio-Access Networks
problem: Designing high-performance many-core SDR processors for baseband processing requires functional validation and end-to-end performance analysis within realistic wireless environments, but RTL simulation is prohibitively slow.
motivation: 5G and beyond wireless standards demand evolving baseband processing infrastructure; programmable many-core RISC-V designs offer flexibility, but need rapid design-space exploration.
method: Fast simulation framework using static binary translation with approximate timing model of many-core hardware (1024 RISC-V cores), coupled to wireless channel models. Simulates critical physical layer 5G OFDM detection functions. Single-threaded: 9.5s-3min per symbol (3 OOM faster than RTL); parallelizable to 128 threads with 73-121x speedup.
key_novelty: Binary translation-based simulator with fast timing model for rapid end-to-end SDR baseband processor exploration.
contributions: 3 orders of magnitude faster than RTL simulation for 5G OFDM symbol detection
Single-thread simulation: 9.5s-3min depending on MIMO size
Supports design-space exploration of many-core RISC-V SDR processors
Integration with wireless channel models for realistic evaluation

metrics.speedup: 3 OOM faster than RTL; 73-121x with parallelization

limitations: Approximate timing model trade-off vs accuracy; applicability to non-OFDM physical layers unclear.
primary_theme: Fast simulation of many-core RISC-V SDR baseband processors
